findings.aws_reference: AWS DynamoDB API Reference CreateTable ("read and write operations only on an ACTIVE table"), ResourceNotFoundException/ResourceInUseException shape docs in the bundled Smithy model, and the generated doc comments at ops/put_item.rs:247-249 and ops/create_table.rs:210-214.
findings.claim: ANSWER TO THE SPECIFIC QUESTION: NO for item data-plane calls. A just-created table is CREATING (Table::status, now < active_at), and PutItem/GetItem/Query/TransactWriteItems resolve the table through Store::active_table(); a non-serving status is answered with ResourceNotFoundException carrying the fixed message 'Requested resource not found', NOT ResourceInUseException. LinkedIn check #5 ('A call on a new DynamoDB table before it is ACTIVE -> ResourceInUseException') does not name the operation and is NOT established as an AWS data-plane behaviour by this corpus: the bundled AWS Smithy model does not model ResourceInUseException for PutItem, GetItem, Query or TransactWriteItems, and documents ResourceNotFoundException as 'The operation tried to access a nonexistent table or index ... or its status might not be ACTIVE'. ResourceInUseException is modelled as a CONTROL-plane conflict ('You tried to delete a table currently in the CREATING state'); the emulator does return it for several control-plane calls (DDB-02). UNVERIFIED: no live AWS replay in this corpus measures a data-plane call on a CREATING table; the LinkedIn assertion itself was not measured here and could describe a control-plane call.

findings.root_cause: Store::active_table()/active_table_mut() collapse 'table absent' and 'table present but not serving items' into the single store refusal item_resource_not_found() -> RequestError::NotFound('Requested resource not found'), which each operation's lift() maps to its modelled ResourceNotFoundException. TableStatus::serves_items() admits only Active and Updating, so CREATING and DELETING are gated. The item handlers have no ResourceInUseException variant to return, by construction of the modelled error enums.

findings.aws_reference: CreateTable API doc (ops/create_table.rs:87-97): CreateTable returns CREATING, becomes ACTIVE later, DescribeTable is the way to check status. ResourceInUseException shape doc (ops/create_table.rs:210-214). In-repo AWS-recorded behavioural doc 20261109T172142Z:47.
findings.claim: The emulator DOES return ResourceInUseException for several CONTROL-plane calls on a CREATING table: a second CreateTable, DeleteTable, UpdateTable and UpdateTimeToLive. It does NOT do so uniformly: TagResource/UntagResource gate only DELETING, and CreateBackup/UpdateContinuousBackups answer TableNotFoundException (DDB-03). The CREATING window is a hard-coded STATUS_TRANSITION = 3 s, and DescribeTable deliberately sleeps out the remaining span before answering, so a caller following AWS's documented pattern (poll DescribeTable / the table_exists waiter) sees ACTIVE on its first poll; a caller that issues a control-plane call immediately after CreateTable can still observe CREATING. A Cloud Control/CloudFormation-created table is minted with active_at = now, so that path never exposes CREATING at all. Open HIGH doc 20261109T172142Z Cause 4 reports that across 5 freshly created tables the table left CREATING before the first CreateBackup could be issued -- an observation recorded at an older commit, not re-verified at fork head. GH #436 (open) asks for the 3 s wait to be configurable/disableable because each create+delete pair costs at least 6 s.

findings.root_cause: CreateTable sets active_at = now + STATUS_TRANSITION (state.rs:75, create_table.rs:516) and returns a TableDescription derived from Table::status(now) (CREATING). DescribeTable computes creation_settles_in(now) and awaits tokio::time::sleep(left.min(STATUS_TRANSITION)) before re-reading and describing (describe_table.rs:164-188), fast-forwarding the polling client past CREATING. MintedTable::active_at is a per-creating-plane decision (state/table_minting.rs:52-55), so the Cloud Control native table effect mints active_at: at and never starts a transition. Control-plane gates branch on table.status(now) with different error classes per operation.
